parsed.rationale: I disagree with the team's acute STEMI read: this looks like sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm with normal intervals and axis, and the upsloping ST segments in V2–V4 lead into tall T waves without clear J-point elevation at STEMI thresholds, reciprocal ST depression or Q waves, which fits a normal or early repolarization pattern rather than an acute infarct, though a visual read alone can't rule out ischemia, so serial ECGs, troponin and the clinical picture should guide management.
